description: Intent i010 (chardev-ioctl-divisor, snapshot s01) complete with one high-confidence finding. FINDING: drivers/tty/synclink_gt.c:4123-4131, function async_mode(), quote "(info->base_clock % (info->params.data_rate * 16))) {" — a modulo whose divisor is the unvalidated user-supplied MGSL_PARAMS.data_rate scaled 16x in fixed-width arithmetic. Untrusted source: MGSL_IOCSPARAMS ioctl handler set_params() (lines 2527-2546) and compat twin set_params32() (1087-1117) copy_from_user a whole MGSL_PARAMS struct and memcpy it into info->params with zero numeric validation; program_hw() is called immediately. Violated invariant: the only screen is 'info->params.data_rate' (raw ==0 check, line 4123), which validates f's input, not f's output at division width — data_rate=2^28 (0x10000000) passes every gate, yet data_rate*16 wraps to 0 in 32-bit arithmetic (verified by compiled C test: u32 2^28*16 = 0x0; on 64-bit kernels where data_rate is unsigned long the threshold is 2^60, likewise 0), so '%' executes modulo-by-zero → kernel oops/DoS, structurally identical to the drm/amd/pm vega10 seed (8*speed wrap → zero tach divisor). Counterevidence: set_rate() (3832-3843) guards 'if (rate)', so the wrapped products passed at lines 4128/4131 are skipped; the tty termios path (change_params:2475) is capped at enumerated baud rates and cannot reach the wrap — the reachable vector is the ioctl. Also classified: 5 safe candidates (synclink_gt.c:4329/3818/4128 set_rate-guarded scaled rates; iio-trig-hrtimer.c:74 validated divisor; stm32-timer-trigger.c:131 freq!=0 checked) and 2 unresolved (hpet.c:865, stb6100.c:386 — hardware/frontend-sourced divisors with shifted operands, not fully traced within bound). Bounded search: six pattern queries over drivers/{iio,media,hid,input,char,tty,misc}. Limitations: legacy Microgate SyncLink GT PCI hardware required; no runtime reproducer executed (wrap confirmed analytically and by C test under $TMPDIR).
